record.title: The support approximation conjecture for vexillary involutions
record.statement:
Let $I^{\mathsf{vex}}_\infty$ be the set of vexillary involutions, and let $\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{inv}}(z)$, $\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{inv}}^+(z)$, and $\operatorname{supp}(\operatorname{GC}^{\mathsf{O}}_z)$ denote the sets defined in the paper. **Support approximation conjecture.** If $z \in I^{\mathsf{vex}}_\infty$, then

$$
\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{inv}}(z)\subseteq \operatorname{supp}(\operatorname{GC}^{\mathsf{O}}_z) \subseteq \mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{inv}}^+(z).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computational verification for all vexillary $z\in I_{11}$ and extends the preceding containment results; the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Eric Marberg and Jiayi Wen, “On some Grothendieck expansions”, arXiv:2412.18963 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.18963

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

record.title: The normalized BGW-number nesting conjecture
record.statement:
Let $g\ge2$ and let $\mathbf d$ be a partition of $g-1$. Write $C(\mathbf d)$ for the normalized BGW number associated with $\mathbf d$. **Nesting conjecture.**

$$
C(g-1)\le C(\mathbf d)\le C(1^{g-1}).
$$

The inequalities assert that the normalized numbers are bounded by the values for the crudest and finest partitions. They were checked numerically through genus $40$; the assertion for all $g$ remains open.
record.source_name: Jindong Guo, Paul Norbury, Di Yang and Don Zagier, “Combinatorics and large genus asymptotics of the Brézin–Gross–Witten numbers”, arXiv:2412.20388 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.20388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for normalized BGW numbers
record.statement:
Fix $g\ge1$, and order the partitions of $g-1$ first by increasing length and then lexicographically among partitions of equal length, with their nonzero entries arranged in increasing order. Let $C(\mathbf d)$ be the normalized BGW number associated with a partition $\mathbf d$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** The function

$$
\mathbf d\longmapsto C(\mathbf d)
$$

is strictly increasing with respect to this ordering for every $g$.
This refines the nesting conjecture by predicting the complete ordering of the normalized BGW numbers. It is based on computations through genus $40$ and remains open.
record.source_name: Jindong Guo, Paul Norbury, Di Yang and Don Zagier, “Combinatorics and large genus asymptotics of the Brézin–Gross–Witten numbers”, arXiv:2412.20388 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.20388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

record.title: The cardinality conjecture for meta-spaces of sigma-sets
record.statement:
Let $A\in 2^{\mathds{N}^{0}}$ and $B\in 2^{\mathds{N}}$. The meta-space generated from the sigma-set fusion $A\oplus B$ and the corresponding fusion with the antiset $B^{-}$ is

$$
\left\langle 2^{A\oplus B},2^{A\oplus B^{-}}\right\rangle.
$$

**Meta-space cardinality conjecture.** For all such $A$ and $B$,

$$
\left|\left\langle 2^{A\oplus B},2^{A\oplus B^{-}}\right\rangle\right|=2^{|A|}\cdot 3^{|B|}.
$$

The example preceding the conjecture has $|A|=|B|=2$ and yields $36=2^{2}\cdot3^{2}$. The general formula is presented as a conjecture, with no resolution supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Ivan Gatica and Alfonso Bustamente, “σ-Sets and σ-Antisets”, arXiv:2501.00047 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: The even-parameter hook bias conjecture for 2-regular partitions
record.statement:
Let $b_{t,i}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $i$ in all $t$-regular partitions of $n$. **Even-parameter hook bias conjecture.** For even $k\ge 8$, $b_{2,k}(n)\ge b_{2,k+1}(n)$ for all $n\ge 0$ and $n\ne k+1$.

This is a modification of Singh and Barman's conjecture that excludes odd parameters, for which the original assertion fails. The paper reports verification for $8\le k\le 20$ and $n\le 10000$, but the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Wenxia Qu and Wenston J. T. Zang, “On the hook length biases of the 2- and 3-regular partitions”, arXiv:2501.13753 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13753

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2025). “This conjecture was proved by Craig, Dawsey and Han .”

record.title: Herzog's last theorem
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a regular local ring, let $I\subset R$ be a proper ideal, and set $S=R/I$. For an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R\to S$ and an $S$-module $M$, write $T_i(S/R,M)$ for the cotangent modules.

**Herzog's last theorem.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $I$ is a complete intersection.
2. $T_i(S/R,S)=0$ for all $i>1$.
3. $T_i(S/R,S)=0$ for all $i\gg1$.

Herzog posed this conjecture in 1981, and the paper states that it remains open. It predicts that the vanishing of the cotangent modules in all sufficiently high degrees, or in every degree greater than one, characterizes complete intersections in regular local rings.
record.source_name: Antonino Ficarra, “Cotangent functors and Herzog's last theorem”, arXiv:2501.13867 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13867

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “In 1981, J\"urgen Herzog posed the following conjecture, which remains open.”

record.title: Universality conjecture for the 34 listed ternary lattices
record.statement: Consider the $34$ ternary lattices listed in the theorem immediately preceding the conjecture, over the relevant real quadratic fields. A **universal ternary lattice** is a ternary quadratic lattice representing every totally positive element of the ring of integers. **Universality conjecture.** All the $34$ ternary lattices listed in the above theorem are indeed universal. The source gives computational verification of representability bounds for these lattices, but a proof of universality for all $34$ lattices remains open.
record.source_name: Vitezslav Kala, Jakub Krásenský, Dayoon Park, Pavlo Yatsyna and Błażej Żmija, “Kitaoka's Conjecture for quadratic fields”, arXiv:2501.19371 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19371

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Despite all this progress, it is curious that the most influential conjecture in the area remains open.”

record.title: Tuite–Thomas–Chartrand circulant-graph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be the order of a graph, and let a **circulant graph** be a graph whose vertices and adjacency relation are invariant under cyclic translation. Let $\operatorname{mp}(G)$ denote the monophonic position number and $\operatorname{diam}(G)$ the diameter. **Tuite–Thomas–Chartrand's conjecture.** For any $n\geq 11$, there is a circulant graph with order $n$, monophonic position number two, and diameter two.

The construction preceding the conjecture preserves these properties while changing the order; the existence of a circulant example for every $n\geq 11$ remains open.
record.source_name: Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavžar and James Tuite, “The General Position Problem: A Survey”, arXiv:2501.19385 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19385

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Another open problem is given in the following conjectured Nordhaus-Gaddum relation.”

record.title: Kiselev–Kozik conjecture on satisfying sequences for rainbow partite matchings
record.statement:
Let $s,n,k$ be positive integers, and let a sequence $(f_i)_{i=1}^s$ be called **satisfying** when it has the property that any $s$ families in $[n]^k$ whose respective sizes exceed $f_i$ contain a cross-matching. The sequences

$$
f_i=i n^{k-1}
$$

and

$$
f_i=\min\{i+C\sqrt{s\log s},s-1\}n^{k-1},\qquad i=1,\ldots,s,
$$

are satisfying, where $C$ is an absolute constant. **Kiselev–Kozik's conjecture.** The two sequences above are satisfying. The first sequence asserts the sharp asymmetric multipartite analogue of the Aharoni–Howard conjecture, while the second captures the previously observed square-root error term. The Aharoni–Howard conjecture itself was resolved for all $s>470$, but these stronger assertions about satisfying sequences remain open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Andrey Kupavskii and Elizaveta Popova, “Satisfying sequences for rainbow partite matchings”, arXiv:2502.03105 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03105

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

record.title: The most-informative Boolean function conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ be uniformly distributed on the Boolean hypercube, and let $\mathbf{Y}$ be obtained by passing each bit of $\mathbf{X}$ through a binary symmetric channel with crossover probability $p=(1-\rho)/2\in[0,1]$. Let $f:\mathbb{H}^n\mapsto\mathbb{H}$ be a Boolean function, and let $H_2(p)=-p\log_2(p)-(1-p)\log_2(1-p)$ be binary entropy. **The most-informative Boolean function conjecture.** One has

$$
I(f(\mathbf{X});\mathbf{Y})\leq 1-H_2(p).
$$

This conjecture asks which Boolean functions maximize the mutual information through a binary symmetric channel. It is known for balanced Boolean functions in a neighborhood of zero correlation, including $|\rho|\leq 0.44$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Zijie Chen, Amin Gohari and Chandra Nair, “A Differential Equation Approach to the Most-Informative Boolean Function Conjecture”, arXiv:2502.10019 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10019

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

record.title: Equality conjecture for the complexity bounds of the 42 magic-manifold knot families
record.statement:
Let $\{K(i)\}_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be the infinite extension of one of the 42 distinguished families of census knots, with breadth $x$, and let $c(K)$ denote the complexity of the knot. For each family, the constructed triangulations give, for $j>0$, the bound

$$
c\big(K(-x-j)\big)=c\big(K(x-1+j)\big)\leq 9+j.
$$

**Complexity equality conjecture.** The inequality in the bounded-complexity result can be upgraded to equality for all 42 families of knots in this paper.

The equality would establish that the constructed triangulations remain minimal throughout all 42 infinite families, extending the confirmed minimality of the census knots beyond the currently verified cases.
record.source_name: Em K. Thompson, “Triangulations of the `magic manifold' and families of census knots”, arXiv:2503.06198 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0607159](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607159).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06198

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Nath's modulo 192 congruences for partitions with distinct even parts
record.statement:
Let $ped(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts are distinct and odd parts are unrestricted. Equivalently, $ped(n)$ counts partitions with no part divisible by $4$, and its generating function is

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} ped(n)q^n=\frac{(-q^2;q^2)_{\infty}}{(q;q^2)_{\infty}}=\frac{(q^4;q^4)_{\infty}}{(q;q)_{\infty}}.
$$

**Nath's conjecture.** For every $n\geq0$,

$$
ped(225n+43)\equiv ped(225n+88)\equiv ped(225n+133)\equiv ped(225n+223)\equiv0\pmod{192}.
$$

These are conjectured Ramanujan-type congruences for the partition function $ped(n)$; the source reports them as conjectures based on Nath's work, with no resolution supplied.
record.source_name: Hemjyoti Nath and Abhishek Sarma, “Congruences and density results for partitions into distinct even parts”, arXiv:2503.06228 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: A family of modulo 128 congruences for overpartitions with 6-regular nonoverlined parts
record.statement:
Let $\overline{R_6^\ast}(n)$ denote the overpartition function in which the nonoverlined parts are $6$-regular. **Modulo 128 congruence family.** For all $n \geq 0$ and $k \geq 1$, we have

$$
\overline{R_6^\ast}\left(18 \cdot 3^{2k+1} n + \dfrac{153 \cdot 3^{2k} - 1}{4}\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{128}.
$$

This extends the observed modulo $8$ congruence to a family of congruences modulo $128$, building on the preceding conjectured case.
record.source_name: Hemjyoti Nath, Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, “New arithmetic properties for overpartitions where nonoverlined parts are -regular”, arXiv:2503.12145 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12145

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Nath–Saikia–Sarma's quadratic congruence conjecture for $2$-regular $3$-tuple partitions
record.statement:
Let $T_{\ell,k}(n)$ denote the number of $k$-tuple partitions of $n$ whose components are $\ell$-regular partitions, and write $T_2(n)=T_{2,3}(n)$. Let $p\geq 5$ be a prime satisfying

$$
\left(\dfrac{-2}{p}\right)_{L}=-1.
$$

Let $t$ be a positive integer such that $(t,6)=1$ and $p\mid t$. **Nath–Saikia–Sarma's conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$ and $1\leq j\leq p-1$,

$$
T_2\left(9\cdot t^2n+\frac{9\cdot t^2j}{p}+\frac{57\cdot t^2-1}{8}\right)\equiv 0\pmod{6}.
$$

This conjecture extends the authors' preceding congruence for primes $p\equiv5$ or $7\pmod 8$ and $p\nmid n$. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers and Haiyang Wang, “Extending recent work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-tuple -regular partitions”, arXiv:2503.12583 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Eswarathasan–Levine conjecture on the finiteness of divisible harmonic numbers
record.statement:
Let $H_n=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n$ be the $n$th harmonic number. For a prime $p$, let $\nu_p(a)$ denote the $p$-adic valuation of $a$, and define

$$
J_p:=\{n\geq 1:\nu_p(H_n)\geq 1\}.
$$

Thus, $J_p$ consists of those $n$ for which $p$ divides the numerator of $H_n$ in lowest terms.

**Eswarathasan–Levine conjecture.** The set $J_p$ is finite for all primes $p$.

Eswarathasan and Levine computed $J_p$ for $p=3,5,7$ and found it finite in each case. Boyd later established finiteness for all primes $p\leq 547$, apart from possibly $p\in\{83,127,397\}$; the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Leonardo Carofiglio, Giacomo Cherubini and Alessandro Gambini, “On Eswarathasan–Levine and Boyd's conjectures for harmonic numbers”, arXiv:2503.15714 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15714

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Lewis–Marberg skew GQ positivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\lambda/\mu$ be a shifted shape, let $w(\lambda/\mu)$ be the signed permutation associated with it in the source, let $a^C_{w(\lambda/\mu)}(\nu)$ be the corresponding strict decomposition-tableau coefficient, and let $GQ^{(\beta)}_{\lambda/\mu}$ and $GQ_\nu$ denote the skew and ordinary $K$-theoretic Schur $Q$-functions.

**Skew $GQ$ positivity conjecture.** For any shifted shape $\lambda/\mu$,

$$
GQ^{(\beta)}_{\lambda/\mu}=\sum_{\nu}a^C_{w(\lambda/\mu)}(\nu)\cdot GQ_\nu.
$$

This is identified with Conjecture 5.14 of Lewis and Conjecture 4.36 of Marberg. It asserts a positive integer $GQ$-expansion for every skew $GQ$ function and remains open; the paper derives it conditionally from the Type C K-Stanley expansion conjecture.
record.source_name: Joshua Arroyo, Zachary Hamaker, Graham Hawkes and Jianping Pan, “Type C K-Stanley symmetric functions and Kraśkiewicz-Hecke insertion”, arXiv:2503.16641 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16641

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “However, establishing the positivity implied by Conjecture is an open problem, even using geometric methods.”

record.title: The composition-lift conjecture for path-complete Lyapunov functions
record.statement:
Let $d4a2,d4a2$ be path-complete Lyapunov functions in $d52f\mathrm{pc}(\Sigma)$ satisfying Assumption~. Suppose that $d53d$ is a subset of linear invertible maps. The **composition-lift conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $d4a2^{\circ}$ simulates $d4a2$.
2. $d4a2\leq_{\mathcal{V},\mathcal{F}}d4a2$ for every template $d4a2$ closed under forward composition with the class of dynamics $d53d$.

This conjecture concerns whether simulation by the composition lift is exactly characterized by the corresponding preorder for every forward-composition-closed template. It was expected in work on composition lifts and is identified in the source with Conjecture 8.20 of Debauche (2024); the supplied material does not establish its resolution.
record.source_name: Wouter Jongeneel and Raphaël M. Jungers, “Ordering and refining path-complete Lyapunov functions through composition lifts”, arXiv:2503.18189 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Modular-three congruences for overcubic partitions
record.statement:
Let $\bar a_m(n)$ denote the overcubic partition function indexed by $m$, as in the paper. For every $n\geq 0$ and $i\geq 1$, the following congruences are conjectured:

**Overcubic partition congruence conjecture modulo powers of three.**

$$
\bar a_{3i+2}(9n+2)\equiv 0 \pmod{6},\qquad \bar a_{9i+5}(9n+3)\equiv 0 \pmod{12},
$$

$$
\bar a_{9i+8}(9n+3)\equiv 0 \pmod{12},\qquad \bar a_{3i+2}(9n+5)\equiv 0 \pmod{6},
$$

$$
\bar a_{3i+2}(9n+8)\equiv 0 \pmod{6}.
$$

The conjecture concerns congruences modulo a prime other than the powers of $2$ studied in detail elsewhere in the paper, and the source suggests that its proof should be similar to the proof of the cited theorem.
record.source_name: Hirakjyoti Das, Saikat Maity and Manjil P. Saikia, “Arithmetic Properties of Generalized Cubic and Overcubic Partitions”, arXiv:2503.19399 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19399

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: The dimension growth conjecture for smooth projective hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 4$ and $d\geqslant 3$. Let $X$ be a smooth projective hypersurface defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$. Let $N(X,B)$ count the rational points on $X$ of height at most $B$.

**Dimension growth conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
N(X,B)\ll_{n,d,\varepsilon} B^{n-2+\varepsilon}.
$$

The paper states that this bound should hold for all $n\geqslant 4$ and $d\geqslant 3$. It is known in particular when $d\geqslant 50$ or $n\geqslant 28$, while the stated range remains open in general; the bound fails in general for $d\leqslant 2$ or $n\leqslant 3$.
record.source_name: Matteo Verzobio, “Counting rational points on smooth hypersurfaces with high degree”, arXiv:2503.19451 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19451

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “The conjecture remains open for $d=3$: however, Salberger proved that it holds if the error term is allowed to depend on $X$ .”

record.title: Existence threshold conjecture for regular link-irregular graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. It is **link-irregular** if $G[N(u)]$ and $G[N(v)]$ are non-isomorphic for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v$, where $N(u)$ denotes the neighborhood of $u$ and $G[N(u)]$ the subgraph induced by that neighborhood. A graph is **regular** if all vertices have the same degree. **Existence threshold conjecture.** There exists a regular link-irregular graph on $n$ vertices if and only if $n\geq 12$. The paper establishes that no regular link-irregular graph exists for $n\leq 9$, extending earlier nonexistence results for regularities $0,1,2,3,4$. The conjectured threshold at $12$ remains open.
record.source_name: Alexander Bastien and Omid Khormali, “On the Regularity, Planarity and Edge Bounds of Link-irregular Graphs”, arXiv:2503.21916 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21916

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Vector-chromatic p-energy lower-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $p\geq 2$, and let $\chi_v(G)$ denote its vector chromatic number. Let $\mathcal{E}_p^+(G)$ and $\mathcal{E}_p^-(G)$ denote its positive and negative $p$-energies. **Vector-chromatic p-energy conjecture.** For all $p\geq 2$,

$$
\chi_v(G)\geq 1+\max\left\{\frac{\mathcal{E}_p^+(G)}{\mathcal{E}_p^-(G)},\frac{\mathcal{E}_p^-(G)}{\mathcal{E}_p^+(G)}\right\}^{\frac{1}{p-1}}.
$$

This would extend the established lower bounds for the vector chromatic number at $p=2$ and $p=\infty$. The supplied text gives counterexamples for the analogous range $0\leq p\leq 1.154$, but does not resolve the conjecture for $p\geq 2$.
record.source_name: Clive Elphick, Quanyu Tang and Shengtong Zhang, “A Spectral Lower Bound on Chromatic Numbers using p-Energy”, arXiv:2504.01295 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01295

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: All-pairs plane Hamiltonian path conjecture for simple drawings
record.statement: Let $K_n$ be drawn simply in the plane, and let $a,b$ be two vertices. A path is **plane** if no two of its edges cross. **All-pairs Hamiltonian-path conjecture.** For every simple drawing of $K_n$ and every choice of two vertices $a,b$, there is a plane Hamiltonian path from $a$ to $b$. The conjecture is verified for $n\leq 10$ in simple drawings and for $n\leq 13$ in generalized twisted drawings, and is proved for several subclasses; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Helena Bergold and Manfred Scheucher, “Investigating Simple Drawings of K_n using SAT”, arXiv:2504.02650 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02650

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: Hoffmann–Tóth convex matching conjecture for simple drawings
record.statement: Let $K_n$ have a convex drawing, and let $M$ be a **plane matching**, meaning a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges no two of which cross. **Hoffmann–Tóth convex-matching conjecture.** For every plane matching $M$ in a convex drawing of $K_n$, there exists a plane Hamiltonian cycle that does not cross any edge from $M$. The conjecture is verified for $n\leq 11$ by the paper's computations, but remains open beyond that range.
record.source_name: Helena Bergold and Manfred Scheucher, “Investigating Simple Drawings of K_n using SAT”, arXiv:2504.02650 (2025).

record.title: Wolstenholme's higher-power congruences for Gaussian integers
record.statement:
Let $i^2=-1$. For an integer $k\geq 1$ and a prime $p>17$, define

$$
S_p^{(k)}=\sum_{\substack{1\leq n,m\leq p-1\\(p,n^2+m^2)=1}}\frac{1}{(mi+n)^k}.
$$

Define $m(k)$ by

$$
m(k)=\begin{cases}4 & \text{if } k\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\3 & \text{if } k\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\2 & \text{if } k\equiv 3\pmod 4,\\1 & \text{if } k\equiv 0\pmod 4.\end{cases}
$$

**Wolstenholme's higher-power congruences.** For every such $k$ and $p$,

$$
S_p^{(k)}\equiv 0\pmod {p^{m(k)}}.
$$

Equivalently, the source writes $m(k)=4-(k-1)\pmod 4$. Computations establish the corresponding congruences for $k$ through $12$, but a general proof is not known; the difficulty is obtaining a general formula for the coefficient of the lowest power of $p$ in the relevant numerator.
record.source_name: Nikita Kalinin, “Wolstenholme's theorem over Gaussian integers”, arXiv:2504.07978 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1211.4570](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4570).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07978

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: The classification conjecture for nearly-Ramsey triples
record.statement:
Let a triple $(d_1,d_2,d_3)$ be **nearly-Ramsey** if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every two-colouring of the circle contains a monochromatic $\varepsilon$-close copy of the triple. **Classification conjecture for nearly-Ramsey triples.** The triple $(d_1,d_2,d_3)$ is nearly-Ramsey if and only if it is one of

$$
\left(\frac47,\frac27,\frac17\right),\quad\left(\frac58,\frac14,\frac18\right),\quad\left(\frac34,\frac16,\frac1{12}\right),\quad\left(\frac7{12},\frac14,\frac16\right),
$$

or is a triple with $d_1=\frac12$. The listed triples and the $d_1=\frac12$ family are proved to be nearly-Ramsey in the paper; the conjecture is that no others exist.
record.source_name: Gábor Damásdi, Nóra Frankl, János Pach and Dömötör Pálvölgyi, “Monochromatic configurations on a circle”, arXiv:2504.10687 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10687

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2025). “The case $k=3$ was settled a long time ago by Bialostocki and Nielsen , and it is not hard to verify the case $k=4$ either.”

record.title: Atkin–O'Brien partition congruence conjecture for powers of 13
record.statement:
Let $P(N)$ be defined by $P(N)=p(n)$ when $N=24n-1$, and $P(N)=0$ if $N<-1$, if $N\not\equiv -1\pmod{24}$, or if $N$ is nonintegral. Let $\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)$ denote the Jacobi symbol. **Atkin–O'Brien partition congruence conjecture.** Let $\alpha\geq 1$ and let $p\neq 13$ be a prime with $p\geq 5$. Then there exists a constant $k=k(p,\alpha)$ such that, for all $N$, 

$$
P(p^2\cdot 13^\alpha N)-\left\{k-\left(\frac{-3\cdot 13^\alpha N}{p}\right)p^{-2}\right\}P(13^\alpha N)+p^{-3}P\left(\frac{13^\alpha N}{p^2}\right)\equiv 0\pmod{13^\alpha}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture was made by Atkin and O'Brien and proves it, so the congruence is no longer open.
record.source_name: Frank Garvan and Zhumagali Shomanov, “A simple proof of the Atkin-O'Brien partition congruence conjecture for powers of 13”, arXiv:2504.10824 (2025).

record.title: Conjecture on knot Floer homology of prime fibered positive knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a prime fibered positive knot of genus $g$, and let $\widehat{HFK}_{-1}(K,g-1)$ denote its knot Floer homology in Alexander grading $g-1$ and Maslov grading $-1$, with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}$. **The knot Floer homology conjecture.**

$$
\widehat{HFK}_{-1}(K,g-1)\cong\mathbb{F}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by computations for prime fibered positive knots with at most 14 crossings and by constraints from the Kauffman state model. Whether the assertion holds for all prime fibered positive knots remains open.

record.title: The subgroup-counting conjecture with the arithmetic-function exponent
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a finite group, and let $T\leq R$ be a subgroup. Define

$$
\operatorname{Sub}(R,T)=\{H\leq R: T\leq H\}.
$$

For a non-zero integer $n$, let $\lambda(n)$ denote the number of prime divisors of $n$, counted with multiplicities. **Subgroup-counting conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for every finite group $R$ and subgroup $T\leq R$,

$$
|\operatorname{Sub}(R,T)|\leq [R:T]^{\lambda([R:T])+c}.
$$

The theorem preceding this conjecture gives the bound $7.3722\,[R:T]^{\frac{\log_2 [R:T]}{4}+1.8919}$, and the conjecture proposes replacing the logarithmic exponent term by $\lambda([R:T])$. The claim is presented as an expected improvement and its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

record.title: The sparsest minimal-graph conjecture
record.statement:
For a positive integer $\ell$, let an $\ell$-minimal graph mean a graph that is minimal at Lovász–Schrijver rank $\ell$. Let $\hat{\mathcal{K}}_{\ell+2,\ell-1}$ denote the specified class of sparse stretched cliques.

**Sparsest minimal-graph conjecture.** For every positive integer $\ell$, a sparsest $\ell$-minimal graph is a sparse stretched clique in $\hat{\mathcal{K}}_{\ell+2,\ell-1}$.

The conjecture generalizes the observed structure of the sparsest 4-minimal graphs, all 40 of which were found to be sparse stretched cliques in $\hat{\mathcal{K}}_{6,3}$. Its validity for arbitrary positive integer $\ell$ remains open.

record.title: The universal quadratic refinement of Sendov's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\beta\in[0,1]$, let $S(\beta)$ be the set of polynomials of degree at least $2$ with complex coefficients, all roots in the closed unit disk, and at least one root at $\beta$, and let $d(P,\beta)$ be the distance from $\beta$ to the closest root of $P'$. **The universal quadratic refinement conjecture.** There is a constant $c\approx0.233$ such that, for every $P\in S(\beta)$,

$$
d(P,\beta)\le1-c\beta(1-\beta).
$$

This is the paper's experimentally motivated conjecture for arbitrary degree and arbitrary root configurations, and would provide a uniform strengthening of Sendov's conjecture. It remains open.

record.title: The $D^2_n$ non-TRVG conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D^2_n$ denote the graph in the paper with parameter $a=2$ and $n$ vertices. A **non-TRVG** is a graph that is not a transparent rectangle visibility graph. The conjecture concerns integers satisfying

$$
n\ge 10.
$$

**The $D^2_n$ non-TRVG conjecture.** $D^2_n$ is a non-TRVG when $n\ge10$.

The paper shows that $D^2_n$ is a TRVG for $n\le 8$ and gives a toroidal representation for $D^2_{10}$, while reporting no planar representation; the asserted non-TRVG result for all $n\ge10$ remains open.

record.title: Non-fiberedness conjecture for non-trivial 2-plat 2-knots
record.statement:
Let $F(p,q)$ be a 2-plat 2-knot, and call it **non-trivial** when it is not the trivial 2-knot. A 2-knot is **fibered** if its complement fibers over the circle with fiber a compact $3$-manifold.

**Non-fiberedness conjecture.** Every non-trivial 2-plat 2-knot is non-fibered.

Computer calculations show that every 2-plat 2-knot $F(p,q)$ with $1 < p \leq 2000$ has a non-monic Alexander polynomial, while fibered ribbon 2-knots of 1-fusion have monic Alexander polynomials. The conjecture asserts that this obstruction holds for all non-trivial 2-plat 2-knots.

record.title: Uniqueness of the degree greater than one morphism from $X_0(p)$
record.statement:

is the only non-constant rational morphism of degree $d>1$ from $X_0(p)$ to a curve of genus at least $2$. record.title: Kusner's 16π-conjecture for sphere eversions
record.statement:
A **sphere eversion** is a regular homotopy $H:\mathbb{S}^2\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^3$ connecting two round spheres of opposite orientation. **Kusner's 16π-conjecture.** There exists a sphere eversion $H$ satisfying, for every $t\in[0,1]$,

$$
W(H_t)\leq 16\pi.
$$

Every sphere eversion must reach Willmore energy at least $16\pi$ because it has a quadruple point at some time and the Li--Yau inequality applies. Whether the lower bound is attainable by an optimal sphere eversion is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Bickle–White conjecture on attaining the genus-sum lower bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\overline{G}$ be its complement, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote the genus of $G$. For $n\geq 11$, consider the lower bound

$$
\left\lceil \frac{1}{12}\left(n^{2}-13n+24\right)\right\rceil
$$

for $\gamma(G)+\gamma(\overline{G})$. **Bickle–White conjecture.** For every $n\geq 11$, there is a graph $G$ for which

$$
\gamma(G)+\gamma(\overline{G})=\left\lceil \frac{1}{12}\left(n^{2}-13n+24\right)\right\rceil.
$$

Bickle and White established the lower bound and showed that it is attained for orders $n=12s+11$ and $n\in\{13,25,37,49\}$; Sun later showed attainment for $n=24s+13$. The conjecture asks for attainment at every order $n\geq 11$.

record.title: The bounded-chaos conjecture for a rigorous EMCHS outcome
record.statement:
Let $\chi$ be the chaotic map used in the EMCHS model, let $y_0\in[0,1]$, and let $\rho(y)$ denote the proposed invariant density. For a suitable class of functions $g$, **bounded-chaos conjecture.** The averages

$$
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N}g(\chi^n(y_0))
$$

converge to

$$
\int_0^1g(y)\rho(y)\,dy
$$

uniformly in $y_0$. Assuming this conjecture together with the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, an implementation of EMCHS would yield infinitely many prime gaps at most $200$. The proposed result is a speculative route to rigor: neither the stated bounded-chaos input nor the resulting prime-gap conclusion is established in the source.

record.title: Nontriviality conjecture for the classes $X_{4k+2}$
record.statement:
For every $k=1,2,\dots$, let

$$
X_{4k+2}=\pi\bigl([\hat L_{4k+1},\sigma_{4k+1}]\bigr)_{4k+2},

where $X_{4k+2}$ is the trivalent leading term described in the source, and let $\mathsf{GC}_2^{4k+2\text{-loop}}$ denote the corresponding loop-order component of the graph complex.

**Nontriviality conjecture.** For every $k=1,2,\dots$, the element $X_{4k+2}$ defines a non-trivial cohomology class in

$$
H^{4k-1}\bigl(\mathsf{GC}_2^{4k+2\text{-loop}}\bigr).

The conjecture has been checked for $k=1$ and $k=2$. In particular, the class $X_{10}$ generates $H^7(\mathsf{GC}_2^{10\text{-loop}})$ in the checked case and survives to the stated spectral-sequence page; the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Indecomposability conjecture for the modules $\widehat{V}$ and $\widehat{W}$
record.statement:
Let $\widehat{\mathfrak{b}}$ be the algebra whose modules are under consideration, and let $\widehat{V}$ and $\widehat{W}$ be the $\widehat{\mathfrak{b}}$-submodules appearing in the decomposition

$$
\widetilde{V}(\mathbf{M},\mathbf{s},c_L,c_M)\cong\widehat{V}\oplus\widehat{W}
$$

of the massive module under the condition

$$
\mathbf{M}+\frac{n^2-1}{24}c_M\neq 0
$$

for every positive integer $n$. **Indecomposability conjecture.** The $\widehat{\mathfrak{b}}$-modules $\widehat{V}$ and $\widehat{W}$ are indecomposable. This conjecture concerns the internal structure of the two summands in the decomposition of the massive module; their indecomposability remains an avenue for further study.

record.title: Optimality conjecture for the Mayer-Erdős phenomenon on similarly ordered Farey fractions
record.statement:
Let $\frac{a_1}{b_1},\frac{a_2}{b_2},\ldots$ be the Farey sequence of order $n$, and let $f(n)$ denote the least positive integer $r$ such that some pair of fractions $r$ positions apart is not similarly ordered. For $d=1,2,2,4$ according as $n\equiv 0,1,2,3\pmod{4}$, the upper bound is expected to be sharp. **Optimality conjecture.** For all $n\geq 4$,

$$
f(n)>\frac{n}{4}.
$$

More precisely, for all $n\geq 92$,

$$
f(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\right\rfloor+d.
$$

Here $d$ is defined by the residue class of $n$ modulo $4$ as above. The claim concerns the eventual optimality of the proven upper bound for the first non-similarly ordered pair of Farey fractions; the stated threshold and equality are supported by computer calculations in the source, but no proof or resolution is supplied.

record.title: Conjecture on the number of terms in the polynomials \(\psi_n\)
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}(n)$ be the partition function for $n\geq 1$, and define

$$
\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(n)=\sum_{\nu=1}^{n}\mathcal{P}(\nu).
$$

For a polynomial $f$, let $\# f$ denote its number of terms. The polynomials $\psi_n$ are the recursively defined polynomials introduced in the paper.

**Term-count conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
\#\psi_n=\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(n).
$$

The preceding theorem proves only the upper bound $\#\psi_n\leq\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(n)$. Computations through $n=30$ support equality, but cancellations among terms of different signs could occur for larger $n$.

record.title: Dasappa et al.'s congruence conjecture for the restricted partition function K
record.statement:
Let $K(n)$ be defined by its generating function

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0}K(n)q^n=f_1^2f_2^2f_7^2f_{14}^2,
$$

where $f_k=(q^k;q^k)_\infty$ and $(a;q)_\infty=\prod_{i\geq 0}(1-aq^i)$. **Dasappa et al.'s conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$ and $\alpha\geq 1$, we have

$$
K(7^\alpha n+7^\alpha-2)\equiv 0 \pmod{7^\alpha}.
$$

This conjecture concerns an infinite family of congruences for a restricted color partition function introduced by Pushpa and Vasuki. The source paper states that it proves this conjecture.

record.title: Singer's injectivity conjecture for the algebraic transfer
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr A$ be the Steenrod algebra over $\mathbb F_2$, and let $Tr_q(\mathbb F_2)$ denote the algebraic transfer in homology degree $q$.

**Singer's conjecture.** The homomorphism

$$
Tr_q(\mathbb F_2)
$$

is one-to-one for every $q$.

Singer's conjecture concerns injectivity of the algebraic transfer, a map relating coinvariants in the cohomology of elementary abelian 2-groups to $\operatorname{Ext}$ over the Steenrod algebra. It is known in low homological degrees, including $q=3$ and $q=4$, but the paper states that it fails in bidegree $(6,6+36)$, so the conjecture is refuted.

record.title: Saikia's parity and 2-adic congruence conjecture for overpartition prime-tuples
record.statement:
Let $\overline{p}_{q}(n)$ denote the number of overpartition $q$-tuples of $n$, where $q$ is prime. **Saikia's conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$ and primes $q$, 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+1)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+2)&\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+3)&\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+4)&\equiv 0 \pmod{2},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+5)&\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+6)&\equiv 0 \pmod{8},\\
\overline{p}_{q}(8n+7)&\equiv 0 \pmod{32}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These congruences extend known arithmetic properties of overpartition tuples and were proposed by Saikia; their general validity remains open.

record.title: The genus bound for the theta knot invariant
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot and let $g(K)$ denote its genus. The Laurent polynomial $\theta(K)$ has degree in $T_1$ satisfying

$$
\deg_{T_1}\theta(K)\leq 2g(K).
$$

record.title: The torsion polynomial conjecture for lens spaces
record.statement:
Let $L(p,q)$ be a lens space with $p$ prime and $p\ge3$, and let $\tau(p,q)$ denote its associated torsion invariant. The homeomorphism classification identifies parameters precisely along the orbits $\{\pm q^{\pm1}\}$.

**Torsion-polynomial conjecture.** For every prime $p\ge3$, the map $q\mapsto \tau(p,q)$ is constant precisely on the orbits $\{\pm q^{\pm1}\}$. Equivalently, $\tau(p,q)$ distinguishes the homeomorphism classes of lens spaces $L(p,q)$.

The invariant is already known to depend only on the homeomorphism-class orbit, and computations up to $p\le 400$ support the converse. Whether it separates all such orbits in general remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on generators with nonsquare quadratic translate over finite fields
record.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and write $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^{*}$ for the multiplicative group of nonzero residue classes modulo $p$. A residue class $\overline{k}$ is a generator if it generates this group, and a residue class is a square modulo $p$ if it is a square in $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^{*}$. **The generator–nonsquare conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$, there exists a generator $\overline{k}$ of $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^{*}$ such that $\overline{k}^{2}+\overline{4}$ is not a square modulo $p$. The conjecture was verified computationally for all primes between $3$ and $2\,000\,000$, but no general proof is given.
